stories.headline: 3 ways Browns QB Shedeur Sanders can show growth vs. Saints
stories.summary: The opportunity is a big one as the second-year quarterback's first start of the season comes at a critical time.
stories.body:
Before Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken announced on Aug. 24 that he was naming Deshaun Watson the team's starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders, he spoke with Sanders in his office about his forward-looking approach.

Ten weeks later, Sanders is poised to make his first start of the 2026 NFL season Sunday at the New Orleans Saints (1 p.m. ET, CBS) as Watson remains sidelined in the NFL's concussion protocol.

"He's very diligent and he likes to play football, has a natural confidence about him," Monken said Friday. "Just like any young player, they've got to play. ... Where he's improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections. There were so many things he needed to work on, and he's done that like any young player. Any young player has a lot to work on, especially at the quarterback position.

"And you can see that from the moment we got here and that's why we opened up the competition and we split the reps was because of his ascent."

Sanders' first start of the season comes at a critical time. The Browns are 5-3 after a Week 8 road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that knocked Cleveland out of first place in the AFC North. ESPN Analytics gives the Browns a 16.5% chance of making the playoffs. A win against the Saints would increase their odds to 25.4% ahead of four straight home games.

Sanders made seven starts as a rookie last season and went 3-4 in those games, but he posted a 19.0 Total QBR, the fifth-lowest mark among 696 quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts in a season in the QBR era (since 2006). He has spent the first eight weeks of the regular season as the backup, getting minimal practice reps, but he has familiarity with the starting offense after splitting reps with Watson in the quarterback competition during training camp.

"I'm just excited to see him go play and hopefully let it rip, which I think he'll do," Browns offensive coordinator Travis Switzer said this week. "He did it [Wednesday] in practice. Go lead, be in command, which I think he's grown tremendously in that area, really since we got here.

"And I think Monk[en] mentioned this the other day, but when you're going through training camp, and we were splitting, and really all the spring, we were splitting a lot of those reps as we were going through all the installs, and we were able to see him in a lot more reps than probably a typical backup would be, because obviously we were finding out who our quarterback was going to be. So, hopefully he can review back to some of those things if it were to be him, and yeah, let it rip. Play with confidence."

Coaches and teammates have praised Sanders' growth in recent months. In New Orleans, he will get the opportunity to display that progression and lead a struggling offense that ranks 29th in points per game (17.4).

Here are the three ways Shedeur Sanders can showcase his progress:

Playing within structure
The tendency for Sanders to hold on to the ball has been a talking point since his time at Colorado. Sanders has acknowledged he tends to hold the ball in efforts to make a big play -- sometimes to his own detriment. As a rookie, Sanders averaged 3.24 seconds to throw, the slowest among 38 quarterbacks who made at least six starts in 2025.

In August, Monken highlighted Sanders' growth in striking a balance between playing within structure and also making plays by holding on to the ball.

"Being able to check the ball down and get it out of his hands; he's such a playmaker that that's hard for him," Monken said. "For a guy that is always looking to make a play, super competitive, that is a win. Trying to get super competitive quarterbacks to understand that throwing the ball away and eliminating lost yardage plays is a win."

In 25 dropbacks across two games in the preseason, Sanders had an average time to throw of 3.10 seconds, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The Browns have the fifth-most yards after catch in the NFL (1,019) this season.

Getting the ball to pass catchers in the flow of the offense plays a big role in that. It also helps to prevent sacks. Watson has taken the most sacks in the league (33), in part because he has held the ball for too long at times.

Taking care of the ball

Sanders threw 10 interceptions from Weeks 11 to 18 last season, which led all quarterbacks in the league during that time frame. Not every pick was the result of a bad decision or throw; some were caused by dropped passes or batted balls.

But at times, Sanders played a risky brand of football that lent itself to turnovers. He had four dropped interceptions from Weeks 11 to 18, twice as many as the next-closest quarterback during that same time span, according to ESPN Research, and tied for the most by any player all of last season.

This season, Watson has only thrown three interceptions, but he has seven fumbles, which leads all quarterbacks, and has lost three fumbles.

Pre-snap operation

A major point of emphasis for Monken during the quarterback competition was the pre-snap operation. Monken heaps plenty of responsibility on his QBs to get the offense in and out of the huddle properly, make the correct adjustments at the line of scrimmage, use cadence correctly and limit pre-snap penalties.

The latter has been an issue for Cleveland through eight games. According to ESPN Research, the Browns have five delay of game penalties, tied for the fifth most in the league, as well as five illegal formation penalties, which are tied for the fourth most. Not all of those infractions fall on the quarterback, but it is largely their responsibility to take control of the pre-snap operation and "eliminate anxiety," in the words of Monken.

When asked to assess Sanders' brief three plays against Pittsburgh while Watson was checked for a concussion, Monken alluded to "a couple plays he could have helped us out with a check" but added that it was unfair to grade Sanders with such limited practice reps.

A raucous environment at the Caesars Superdome will provide a tough test for Sanders, but coaches have said they don't anticipate needing to adjust the game plan or pre-snap operation with Sanders under center.

"The more anxiety that we can relieve pre-snap, which usually comes down to the play clock, just having as much time as possible before the play clock to allow us to operate and relieve that anxiety, I think that's going to be huge," Switzer said.

"As far as the snap count goes, when we're in the gun we'll be in silent [count], and we've been in silent every road game this year. So that part I don't think is really a whole lot different, but certainly just trying to put a premium, like we always do, but especially this week with them being indoors and it being a loud place, we talk about the four twos. Our pre-snap, in and out of the huddle. Shortening calls as a staff as much as we possibly can.

"Monk[en] will talk about getting the play in as fast as possible, which he always tries to do. All those things are certainly at a premium when you play at a place like that," Switzer said.

stories.headline: Fantasy adds, NBA bets to make for Friday: Cam Spencer, Saddiq Bey stand out
stories.summary: Andre Snellings breaks down Friday's NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
stories.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Friday
The NBA enters the weekend with a nine-game slate of NBA Cup Group Play games. The marquee game in the early window of games is the Philadelphia 76ers on the road against the Cleveland Cavaliers. In addition to two of the best teams in the East facing off, it's always fun to see LeBron James return to Cleveland.

The middle window features two of the Western Conference teams with only two losses facing off, with the surprising Memphis Grizzlies hosting the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Thunder have been devastated by early season injuries, but they've still righted the ship enough to play winning basketball around Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

In the late slot, the 7-2 Los Angeles Lakers play host to the 6-1 Portland Trail Blazers. The Lakers are 4-1 at home, but the Trail Blazers are an undefeated 5-0 on the road, so something will have to give in tonight's matchup.

These and many other storylines will be on display tonight. As we do, let's dig deeper into the matchups to identify some fantasy streamer options and betting angles of interest.

Fantasy stream team

Available in at least 50% of ESPN leagues

Saddiq Bey, SF/PF, New Orleans Pelicans (rostered in 25.1% of ESPN leagues)

Bey is one of the better shooters/scorers on the Pelicans, and he seems to have found his groove off the bench. Over his past three outings, Bey has averaged 21.7 PPG, 5.0 RPG, 2.0 SPG and 1.7 3PG in 30.3 MPG as a sixth man.

Jrue Holiday, PG/SG, Trail Blazers (45.3%)

Holiday is a big reason for why the Trail Blazers have played so well of late and lead the Western Conference going into tonight's game with the Lakers. He has taken on a more prominent role with Ja Morant injured, and over his past three games has averaged 15.3 PPG, 5.3 RPG and 4.3 APG in just under 24 MPG off the bench.

Cam Spencer, SG/PG, Grizzlies (10.7%)

While Ty Jerome has been an amazing scorer for the Grizzlies to start the season, Spencer has quietly been making his mark in the backcourt as well. He has at least seven assists in four straight games despite averaging only 25.5 MPG off the bench. He also remains a long-range shooting threat that contributes positively in points and rebounds as well.

Kingston Flemings, SG/PG, Atlanta Hawks (6.6%)

Flemings moved into the starting lineup for the Hawks on Wednesday, pushing CJ McCollum to the bench. He responded with 14 points, four assists and three rebounds in 23 minutes, his third double-digit scoring effort in his last four games. He has also notched at least four assists in five straight games and had a four-steal outing last week.

Dre's best bets for Friday

Philadelphia 76ers -2.5 (-110) at Cleveland Cavaliers

The 76ers have the best record in the NBA and have yet to lose a game in which their starting five have all played together. None of their five starters are on the injury report for tonight's game. The 76ers beat the Cavaliers by eight points when they played earlier this season and enter this game on a five-game winning streak with no win by fewer than five points. The Cavaliers, on the other hand, have lost three of their last four games with each loss by at least three points.

Saddiq Bey 13+ points (-107)

Bey is in the midst of his best scoring streak of the season, with three straight games of at least 18 points scored while averaging 21.7 PPG over that stretch. He has scored at least 13 points in six of his eight games this season, and the Pelicans will rely on his scoring tonight against a strong opponent in the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Cam Spencer 5+ assists (-159)

Spencer made his name last season as a 3-point marksman, but he is quietly a strong distributor as well. He has dished at least five assists in five straight games, even in his role off the bench, and in his last four has ramped it up even further with 9.3 APG in that span.

Portland Trail Blazers +3.5 (-116) at Los Angeles Lakers

The Lakers are playing well to open the season with a 7-2 record and a +7.9 average scoring margin, but the Trail Blazers have the best record (6-1) and best scoring margin (+11.2) in the Western Conference thus far. Both teams are led by do-everything point-wings in Luka Doncic and Deni Avdija, respectively, but the Trail Blazers have been getting excellent play from their veteran backcourt of late, with Damian Lillard and Holiday really stepping up. That veteran leadership in the backcourt has led them to a 5-0 road record this season, including a seven-point road win over the Lakers in their first meeting.

stories.headline: Chelsea's Xabi Alonso 'very happy' with Cole Palmer despite England omission
stories.summary: Xabi Alonso said he has no time to spend worrying about international call-ups for his players after Cole Palmer was omitted from the England's Nations League squad.
stories.body:
Xabi Alonso said he has no time to spend worrying about international call-ups for his players after Cole Palmer was omitted from the England's Nations League squad.

The 24-year-old was not amongst the 26 players named by Thomas Tuchel for the matches against Croatia and Spain, following his withdrawal from the squad during the last international break in October.

Tuchel repeated his observation that Palmer "misses too many opportunities" to stake his England claims when he discussed his latest squad on Friday.

He was not selected for the World Cup during the summer following a season that was badly hit by injuries and loss of form.

"Everything takes time but time I'm very happy with his quality and his attitude and his impact on the rest of the team."

Palmer was one of five players to withdraw from October's England squad after it had been announced.

It prompted questions around his commitment to the national team, especially since he started both matches for Chelsea either side of the international break.

Asked whether there was regret that Palmer had not made himself available, Alonso said: "We haven't talked about that. We are focused on our things, on Chelsea things, how to do better, how he can become more and more influential in games. Those are our topics.

"We speak about Chelsea. We speak about us. We have enough on our plate. We have enough to focus on each weekend."

Alonso could have goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez available to return earlier than expected for the game at the Stadium of Light, following his surgery on the fractured jaw sustained during victory at Everton last month.

- Cole Palmer 'misses too many opportunities to impress' - England boss Thomas Tuchel

- Why Cole Palmer is on notice in Tuchel's new-look England: 'The competition is on'

- Romeo Lavia: Meeting Eden Hazard gave me extra motivation to succeed at Chelsea

Should he play, the Argentina international will wear a protective mask over his face, which Alonso joked came from a specialist and "not a Halloween shop."

"[On Saturday] we have the last training session and we will decide," he said. "He's training well. Emi has made a great effort to be back. He's been ahead of the plans to be part of the team."

Moisés Caicedo will undergo a fitness test ahead of the match, although Alonso said it was not due to a recurrence of his recent calf injury.

"After the last game he had a little problem. We expect to check tomorrow. It's a discomfort more than the calf."

stories.headline: George Russell hit with five-place grid penalty for São Paulo Grand Prix
stories.summary: George Russell will face a five-place grid penalty at the São Paulo Grand Prix after his Mercedes team fitted another new engine to his car ahead of this weekend's race at Interlagos.
stories.body:
George Russell will face a five-place grid penalty at the São Paulo Grand Prix after his Mercedes team fitted another new engine to his car ahead of this weekend's race at Interlagos.

Russell's slim hopes of championship glory slipped from his grasp at last weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, where his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1's youngest ever champion.

Power unit reliability has been a weakness of Mercedes this year, with Russell suffering a failure at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia that made this weekend's penalty inevitable.

The issue in Malaysia meant he was forced to take a new power unit -- and grid penalty -- at the following round in Singapore, but with seven races remaining and F1 engines only designed to last six race weekends, he was always expected to take another engine, and therefore another penalty, before the end of the year.

Mercedes opted to take the hit in Brazil as overtaking has historically been easier at the Interlagos circuit than at the other venues remaining on the calendar.

"I mean we always had to take a grid penalty at some point," Russell said in a post on Mercedes' Instagram.

"Obviously we took one in Singapore but from Singapore until the end of the season, we felt this was a good place to take it.

- Kimi Antonelli pays tribute to Ayrton Senna with special São Paulo helmet after 'emotional' family visit

- São Paulo Grand Prix: Lando Norris fastest in first practice in heavily-upgraded McLaren

- George Russell breaks silence on swift Mexico City GP exit: 'Needed to get out of there'

"Obviously, Lewis [Hamilton] had a big grid penalty here a number of years ago [2021] and did pretty well.

"Five places doesn't seem that bad and we'll try and come back through."

Mercedes revealed earlier this week that Antonelli was just a handful of laps away from missing out on his crowning podium finish in Mexico due to an oil leak from a cracked sump on his engine.

The issue meant the Italian has also needed to change his engine in Brazil, but he had enough low mileage components in his existing pool of parts to make the change without incurring a penalty.

stories.headline: NHL Power Rankings: Updated poll, plus fantasy hockey surprises for all 32 teams
stories.summary: Another week with the Canes at No. 1, but a big shakeup in the Top 5.
stories.body:
Through another week of the 2026-27 NHL season, the Carolina Hurricanes remain atop the ESPN Power Rankings. But, there are big changes elsewhere in the top five and beyond.

And as a special treat, this week is another fantasy hockey takeover! Sean Allen (East) and Victoria Matiash (West) identified the biggest fantasy hockey surprise -- either good or bad -- for each team.

It's not too late to play ESPN fantasy hockey, with new leagues starting every Monday.

How we rank: A panel of ESPN hockey commentators, analysts, reporters and editors sends a 1-32 poll based on the games through Wednesday. Those ballots are combined to come up with the rankings you see below.

Note: Previous ranking for each team refers to the previous edition, published on Oct. 30. Points percentages are through Thursday's games.

1. Carolina Hurricanes
Previous ranking: 1

Points percentage: 77.78%

Pyotr Kochetkov, G (4.75 fantasy points per game, 18.2% available): Kochetkov has never finished a full NHL season with a save percentage better than .911. He's at .921 this time, with two shutouts and just one regulation loss, and he has grabbed the bulk of Carolina's starts. Behind a team that allows barely 22 shots a game, this one has legs.

Next seven days: vs. CHI (Nov. 7), vs. SEA (Nov. 12)

2. Minnesota Wild
Previous ranking: 3

Points percentage: 73.53%

Ryan Hartman, C (0.92 FPPG, 68.2% available): As the Wild establish themselves as the early team to track down in the Central Division, Hartman is becoming a casual supporting cast member in John Hynes' otherwise formidable lineup. A depressing state of affairs for fantasy managers accustomed to some production from the feisty forward who, suprisingly, isn't satisfying any categories at present.

Next seven days: vs. SJ (Nov. 6), vs. TB (Nov. 7), @ MTL (Nov. 10), @ TOR (Nov. 12)

3. Edmonton Oilers
Previous ranking: 4

Points percentage: 73.53%

Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, C/LW (2.76 FPPG, 29.4% available): Harkening back a few short weeks, there was minimal fantasy interest in the forward, who put up only mediocre numbers the past two seasons and started this campaign on IR. Fast-forward to now and the longest-serving Oiler of all time is picking up points like it's 2022-23. Skating on a power play with McDavid, Draisaitl and Bouchard certainly doesn't hurt.

Next seven days: vs. VAN (Nov. 7), vs. NYR (Nov. 9), vs. PHI (Nov. 11)

4. Boston Bruins
Previous ranking: 2

Points percentage: 73.53%

James Hagens, C (1.98 FPPG, 62.8% available): The 20-year-old has wasted no time making his rookie season a fantasy story. Hagens is on pace to blow past every scoring mark he has ever set, Boston has dominated at 5-on-5 when he's out with Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt, and he has earned power-play time.

Next seven days: vs. FLA (Nov. 8), vs. MTL (Nov. 12)

5. Tampa Bay Lightning
Previous ranking: 6

Points percentage: 73.33%

Charle-Edouard D'Astous, D (2.00 FPPG, 68.8% available): We flagged D'Astous as a pickup two weeks ago, and he has only strengthened his case. His power-play time has nearly tripled from last season, and he's been on the ice for most of Tampa's power-play time lately. Role-driven production on a contender is the kind that sticks.

Next seven days: @ MIN (Nov. 7), @ WPG (Nov. 8), @ BUF (Nov. 11), @ CBJ (Nov. 12)

6. Vegas Golden Knights
Previous ranking: 5

Points percentage: 66.67%

Rasmus Andersson, D (1.52 FPPG, 13.0% available): He isn't anchoring the top power play -- that's a five-forward crew -- and he isn't leading his club in blocked shots -- that's Noah Hanifin -- so all Andersson is accomplishing right now is serving as a functional second-pair defender with five even-strength points in 17 games. A disappointing surprise.

Next seven days: @ BUF (Nov. 8), vs. UTA (Nov. 11)

7. New Jersey Devils
Previous ranking: 7

Points percentage: 68.75%

Arseny Gritsyuk, LW/RW (1.97 FPPG, 56.6% available): Gritsyuk has the best seat in New Jersey, riding with Jesper Bratt and Jack Hughes, and the trio has dominated the scoreboard at 5-on-5. He's also shooting at more than double his career rate, so expect the goals to slow. The linemates are why he should stay rostered when they do.

Next seven days: @ NYI (Nov. 7), @ TOR (Nov. 8), @ WPG (Nov. 10), vs. WSH (Nov. 12)

8. Montreal Canadiens
Previous ranking: 10

Points percentage: 71.88%

Jacob Fowler, G (4.96 FPPG, 21.0% available): The 21-year-old has turned Montreal's crease into his own, going 7-1-1 with a .925 save percentage and two shutouts, including a 46-save gem against St. Louis. He has taken four of the past five starts, and with the Canadiens winning, the work should keep coming.

Next seven days: @ TOR (Nov. 7), vs. MIN (Nov. 10), @ BOS (Nov. 12)

9. Dallas Stars
Previous ranking: 11

Points percentage: 62.50%

Miro Heiskanen, D (1.82 FPPG, 4.4% available): After a more productive start to the season, the Stars' top defenseman has five assists and zero goals (minus-three) to show for eight consecutive contests. Hardly terrible figures, but a disappointing surprise from what was anticipated from a figure expected to keep pace with some of the best fantasy blueliners in the biz.

Next seven days: vs. SJ (Nov. 7), vs. WPG (Nov. 12)

10. Utah Mammoth
Previous ranking: 8

Points percentage: 61.76%

Sebastian Cossa, G (1.33 FPPG, 98.6% available): He's already proving to be more valuable than Karel Vejmelka for his hockey club and fantasy managers alike. After getting his pro pads wet in his first legitimate shot at regular NHL competition, Cossa is establishing himself as a dependable go-to for a strong Utah club with plenty of talent out front. If the Mammoth don't trade for an upgrade in net, the 23-year-old is going to start piling up positive fantasy points quickly.

Next seven days: @ OTT (Nov. 7), @ VGK (Nov. 11), vs. STL (Nov. 12)

11. Colorado Avalanche
Previous ranking: 15

Points percentage: 58.82%

Scott Wedgewood, G (-1.51 FPPG, 29.2% available): With Mackenzie Blackwood back in form, few expected the Avalanche's other netminder to repeat last year's impressive fantasy showing. But this season's flat-out surprisingly poor play from Wedgewood, when offered the occasional opportunity to start for one of the league's better teams, still inspires a shake of the head.

Next seven days: vs. DET (Nov. 7), @ TOR (Nov. 10), @ OTT (Nov. 12)

12. Florida Panthers
Previous ranking: 9

Points percentage: 62.5%

Seth Jones, D (2.55 FPPG, 13.4% available): Jones is scoring like a point-per-game defender, and nothing about it screams fluke. He's logging more than 24 minutes a night with heavy power-play duty, his shot volume is way up and he's converting at his usual rate. Florida's quarterback is back to being a fantasy cornerstone at 32.

Next seven days: @ WSH (Nov. 7), @ BOS (Nov. 8), @ CBJ (Nov. 10), vs. DET (Nov. 12)

13. Ottawa Senators
Previous ranking: 13

Points percentage: 61.77%

Linus Ullmark, G (5.30 FPPG, 9.4% available): Last season's struggles are a distant memory. Ullmark went 7-1-0 with a .945 save percentage before a lower-body injury landed him on injured reserve in late October. He wasn't expected to be out long, so if a frustrated manager in your league cut him loose, pounce.

Next seven days: vs. UTA (Nov. 7), vs. WSH (Nov. 10), vs. COL (Nov. 12)

14. Seattle Kraken
Previous ranking: 12

Points percentage: 63.33%

Mackie Samoskevich, LW (1.84 FPPG, 92.6% available): While many suspected the young skater would enjoy the chance to further spread his wings away from an exceptionally stacked lineup in Florida, fewer projected he would blossom into a such a valuable fantasy performer so quickly. Skating alongside rising star Berkly Catton, the 23-year-old has three goals and four assists on his past six contests.

Next seven days: vs. NYR (Nov. 7), vs. CAR (Nov. 12)

15. Washington Capitals
Previous ranking: 14

Points percentage: 57.14%

Jordan Kyrou, RW (1.98 FPPG, 33.8% available): Kyrou's scoring has outrun his usage. Fifteen minutes a night and fewer than two shots a game don't usually produce this kind of output, he's shooting well above his career mark and Washington has been outscored with him on the ice at 5-on-5.
